descriptionChirho: A masculine noun denoting fierce rage, fury, or stormy indignation, used of both human anger and natural phenomena personified as wrathful. Applied to the rage of King Asa against the seer (2 Chr 16:10), the fury with which an army was sent home (2 Chr 28:9), the wrath of a king compared to a lion's roaring (Prov 19:12), YHWH's indignation descending in storm-theophany imagery (Isa 30:30), bearing the Lord's indignation (Mic 7:9), and the raging of the sea which ceased when Jonah was thrown overboard (Jonah 1:15). Poetic and late usage; cognate with the verb za'af (to be enraged).
